topIssues.title: op-reth: eth_simulateV1 ignores the EIP-7825 gas cap on OP chains after reth v2.5.2
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Found while reviewing the reth v2.5.2 bump (#22495).

reth v2.5.2's `eth_simulateV1` sets `tx_gas_limit_cap = Some(u64::MAX)` whenever EIP-8037/Amsterdam is off ([`helpers/call.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/blob/0fbe428518594611bdd3fdd822eb5968823c8e66/crates/rpc/rpc-eth-api/src/helpers/call.rs#L147-L151)), not only when `validation: false`. No OP fork maps to Amsterdam ([`spec.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-revm/src/spec.rs#L50)) and OP leaves the cap unset to use revm's spec-derived fallback ([`env.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/env.rs#L123-L127)), so on every Karst+ chain a *validated* simulate accepts a transaction with `gas_limit > 2^24` that block validation rejects. `OpEthApi` inherits the default ([`call.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/eth/call.rs#L7)).

The upstream comment ties EIP-7825 to Amsterdam's accounting, but the cap itself is Osaka, so this looks wrong for L1 Osaka too. Options: upstream-first fix (lift the cap only when `validation` is false, or derive it from the spec), or an OP `simulate_v1` override. Either way `estimate_gas_7825`-style coverage exists for `eth_estimateGas` but not for simulate.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topIssues.title: op-reth: pin OP engine defaults and audit deployments for reth v2.5.2 flag changes
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Found while reviewing the reth v2.5.2 bump (#22495). Operator-facing changes inherited from upstream; op-reth sets no engine defaults of its own.

**Defaults moved** (visible in the CLI snapshot, [`cli.snap`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-reth/crates/cli/tests/snapshots/cli.snap#L250-L252)): `--engine.persistence-threshold` 2 → 7; `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target` default 0 → `min(threshold, 5)`; `--engine.persistence-backpressure-threshold` (still 16) is now measured *beyond* the buffer target, so the stall point moves from 16 to ~21 unpersisted blocks. On 2 s or sub-second OP block times the DB tip lags the head by 5 blocks and up to 7 may be unpersisted: larger crash-recovery redo window and engine memory.

**Startup constraints** (`EngineArgs::validate`): buffer target must not exceed the threshold; masking blocks + buffer must stay below the threshold; `--engine.txpool-prewarming` conflicts with `--engine.disable-state-cache`. A deployment passing e.g. `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target 5 --engine.persistence-threshold 2` now fails to start. `--engine.sparse-trie-max-hot-slots` / `-storage-tries` / `-accounts` were removed (clap rejects them) and the `sparse_trie_retained_memory_bytes` gauge is gone.

**Env-activated flags**: `--engine.txpool-prewarming` and `--engine.sender-recovery-cache` read `RETH_ENGINE_TXPOOL_PREWARMING` / `RETH_ENGINE_SENDER_RECOVERY_CACHE`. The recovery cache is populated by the network component on OP but never read: `OpEvmConfig` recovers senders directly ([`lib.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-reth/crates/evm/src/lib.rs#L325-L331)), unlike `EthEvmConfig`.

**Other**: `reth.toml` `bootnodes` now takes precedence over the superchain-registry bootnodes; RocksDB keeps all files open when `RLIMIT_NOFILE >= 128k`.

Proposed: (1) pin OP-specific engine defaults with `DefaultEngineValues::try_init` ([`engine.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/blob/0fbe428518594611bdd3fdd822eb5968823c8e66/crates/node/core/src/args/engine.rs#L63)) so upstream tuning churn shows up in our diff instead of silently; (2) audit deployed engine flags (k8s, devnets) before rolling out; (3) either wire `SenderRecoveryCache` into `OpEvmConfig` or make the flag a no-op on OP.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topIssues.title: op-revm: make the deposit gas-cap exemption a property of OpHandler::tx_gas
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Found while reviewing the reth v2.5.2 bump (#22495).

Deposits are exempt from the EIP-7825 transaction gas cap. Today that exemption is implemented only in `alloy_op_evm::OpEvm::transact_raw`, which temporarily replaces `cfg.tx_gas_limit_cap` with `u64::MAX` around a deposit ([`lib.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/lib.rs#L363-L376)). `OpHandler` itself does not override the gas split: revm 42 moved `initial_gas_and_reservoir` into a new defaulted `Handler::tx_gas` (`revm-handler` 42.0.1, `handler.rs:215`), called from `run_without_catch_error`, `run_system_call`, `runtime_oog_result` and the inspector path. A consumer driving published `op-revm` directly (`ExecuteEvm::transact`/`replay`/`transact_commit`) therefore hands an oversized deposit `cap - intrinsic` regular gas and parks the rest in the EIP-8037 reservoir, i.e. a spuriously OOG deposit. `op-revm` is a published crate; Flashbots' `op-rbuilder` redirects it to this repo via `[patch.crates-io]`.

Proposed: override `Handler::tx_gas` in `OpHandler` to pass `u64::MAX` for `DEPOSIT_TRANSACTION_TYPE` (next to the existing deposit skip in `validate_env`, [`handler.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs#L89)), then delete the save/restore in alloy-op-evm. The two deposit-cap tests in `alloy-op-evm/src/tests.rs` should keep passing unchanged, plus a new op-revm-level test.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Full rewind deletes backfilled logs and invalidates valid blocks
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** I found this while I reviewed ethereum-optimism/optimism#22846.

A full rewind deletes every chain's logsDB, including the cold-start backfill. The backfill is the history the node needs to verify the timestamps it is about to replay. After the delete, the node invalidates valid blocks.

## Event sequence

1. `buildRewindPlan` returns a plan with a nil `TargetHeads` when `lastTS <= firstVerifiableTimestamp` (`interop.go:953-961`).
2. `applyRewindPlan` then calls `db.Clear()` on every chain (`interop.go:1065-1070`).
3. `clearLocked` deletes the whole range and resets `firstBlock` to 0 (`db.go:474-484`).
4. Verification resumes at the first verifiable timestamp with an empty logsDB.
5. `verifyExecutingMessage` calls `Contains` for an initiating message that the backfill held (`algo.go:229-231`).
6. `Contains` returns `interop.ErrFuture` because `hasBlocks` is false (`db.go:287-289`).
7. `verifyInteropMessages` treats the error as an invalid executing message (`algo.go:129-141`).
8. The round applies `DecisionInvalidate` and replaces a valid block.

## Why the delete is wrong

The logsDB holds history below `firstVerifiableTimestamp` on purpose. `runColdStartBackfill` seals one message expiry window of history before the first verified timestamp (`log_backfill.go:100-166`). A rewind of the verified state to that timestamp does not make the backfill invalid. It is exactly the history the node needs to verify that timestamp again.

## Why the node does not recover

Cold start runs once, from `Start` (`interop.go:333`). `waitingForSync` never returns to true, so no backfill re-runs in process.

A restart repairs the node only if the verifiedDB also emptied. If any commit survives, `tryInitFromVerifiedDB` resumes and skips backfill (`interop.go:342-350`).

## Reachability

The window is narrow. A rewind removes one timestamp per round.

`progressInterop` calls `buildRewindPlan(*obs.LastVerifiedTS)` (`interop.go:736`). `observeRound` sets `LastVerifiedTS` from `verifiedDB.LastTimestamp()` (`interop.go:600-603`). So the plan always targets the last verified timestamp, not a reorg depth. The loop then re-checks `SameL1Chain` on the new last entry (`interop.go:635-643`) and repeats.

The verifiedDB has no pruning. `firstTimestamp` moves only in `Rewind`, and only downward or to empty (`verified_db.go:254-290`). So `first` stays at the first round the node ever verified, for the life of the data directory.

To reach `lastTS <= first`, the node must walk its verified DB back to the single first entry. The L1 reorg must invalidate the L1 inclusion of every verified timestamp. In practice the reorg depth must exceed the age of the verified DB. That gives two reachable cases:

1. A young verified DB. A node that cold-started minutes ago holds a recent `L1Inclusion` on its first entry. An ordinary one or two block L1 reorg reaches past it. If the node has verified exactly one timestamp, `last == first` and any L1 inconsistency triggers the clear at once.
2. After an operator wipes the data directory, which is the documented recovery path. That returns the node to case 1.

A mature node is effectively immune. The reorg would have to be deeper than the whole run.

A rewind to the interop activation timestamp is harmless. `runColdStartBackfill` clamps `commonStart` to `activationTimestamp` (`log_backfill.go:122`), so nothing is retained below activation, and a message cannot reference a pre-activation block anyway.

The damaging case is a node that cold-starts long after activation. `advanceColdStartInit` sets `verificationStartTimestamp` to `max(activation, max_c firstSafeHeadTS)` (`log_backfill.go:31-38`). The backfill below that point is real data, and the clear destroys it.

## Expected behavior

Truncate the logsDB to the last block that backfill sealed, instead of a full delete. Keep every block below `firstVerifiableTimestamp`. Clear the database only when the rewind reaches the interop activation timestamp.

In process, this is sufficient. After the verifiedDB empties, `observeRound` reads `firstVerifiableTimestamp`, which falls back to the unchanged `verificationStartTimestamp` (`interop.go:235-245`). So verification resumes at the same point that backfill ended.

Re-run backfill if the resume point can ever move later than the backfill end. `verifyCanAddTimestamp` rejects a gap larger than one block time (`logdb.go:193-198`), so a later resume point would wedge the seal path.

## Related

- ethereum-optimism/optimism#20627 added `reconcileLogsDBTail` and the backfill-path clear.
- ethereum-optimism/optimism#19287 introduced the L1 reorg rewind handling.
- ethereum-optimism/optimism#22846 covers storage errors that cause invalidation. This issue is a separate cause of the same outcome.

topPRs.title: op-private-interop!: establish the private-chain PoC reference
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Establishes an upstream draft reference for the private-chain interop PoC, including private execution, deterministic public projection, message-position resolution before publication, and persistent LightCL recovery. This is experimental work intended for eventual upstreaming after substantial review and refinement.

Projection spans are admitted as a whole before derivation releases their first new block. A pure Go/Kona validator enforces the transaction grammar, claim framing, per-block private OutputV0 records, and the span proof statement. After invalidation or sequencing-window expiry, publication binds to the canonical public parent and the last surviving private checkpoint, including a commitment to intervening replacement inputs. LightCL checks the local private output against the surviving record before adopting it, then retains its rewind, deposit-only replacement, and restart safeguards.

The verifier remains an explicitly configured insecure stub: publication is operator-attested, and private execution correspondence is not cryptographically verified. Protocol fallback blocks need no publisher proof; a future real proof must cover private execution through their recovery interval. This profile requires fresh deployments with interop and Isthmus active at genesis. Published spans cannot cross future activation blocks under the current rules. Initiating messages retain upstream's strict earlier-timestamp rule; same-timestamp dependencies remain unsupported. Private execution proofs, complete fault-proof execution support, and native ETH bridging/withdrawal settlement remain outside the supported profile.

Validation: targeted Go suites and repository Go lint pass; 662 affected Rust tests, strict clippy, no-std, feature propagation and SP1 guest lock checks pass; 31 private-profile Solidity tests plus three cross-language claim-vector tests pass. A fresh op-up private-interop smoke run passes. The full devstack/sysgo private-interop acceptance run passes all 13 enabled tests in 37m23s, including outage/expiry, invalidation, L1 reorgs, interrupted recovery, and restart after newer valid history. Changed registry artifacts and its interface pass scoped verification. Repository-wide contract tooling also encounters unchanged dispute-game interface mismatches and conflicting duplicate ZK-game build artifacts; those unrelated files are outside this update. The optional production-cadence soaks have not been repeated for this change. Two independent scoped reviews covered derivation parity, recovery, and public-source publication; broader production/security and full-feature reviews remain necessary.

Known existing CI issue: broad acceptance shards previously exposed the ordinary-follow finality guard rejecting stock EL-sync bootstrap snapshots whose follower finalized label is ahead of its source. That guard is unchanged by this update and remains an open issue for the recovery stack. Prior CI results do not establish that this revision is green.

This reference excludes atomic coordinator/shared-block builder work and local deployment artifacts. It does not update running devnet images.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** the new claim wire format, per-block output records, contract bytecode and private genesis-output configuration require matching clients/contracts and fresh databases. Preserve the private recovery journal alongside the private execution database. Unsupported private native bridge routes must remain disabled.

topPRs.title: op-private-interop,contracts!: derive and recover a private ETH chain public projection
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Private interop keeps application execution private while publishing the message history needed by the public interop set. One private-chain genesis produces a deterministic public projection, using standard span-batch transport and cross-chain dependency checks. This replaces #22729 and uses the existing `private-interop/devnet-readiness` branch unchanged at `9f679db23ac12be10049766843495a03eb2993c2`.

Ordinary L1 deposits execute against private state. On the public projection, user deposits are included as successful no-ops with no minting, state changes, execution gas or logs; authenticated system deposits still execute. After sequencing-window expiry, interop invalidation or an L1 reorg, the private node returns to a surviving authenticated checkpoint and rebuilds canonical deposit-only intervals before publication resumes. Recovery ancestry persists across restarts, and batch publication waits for private reconciliation and an authorized batcher epoch.

The PoC remains operator-attested; execution-proof enforcement and private withdrawal settlement are future work. Native ETH bridge routes remain disabled in the private profile. The diff also includes the companion L1 event-certificate contracts, which are separate from the projection mechanism. Versioned bundle tooling, remote private-pair smoke, and deposit/recovery/reorg/rotation/cadence tests support devnet preparation.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** projection deposit execution, the claimed-follow RPC and recovery journal configuration require matching clients/contracts and fresh databases when migrating from earlier prototypes. Configure the persistent recovery path and ordinary projection rollup RPC as documented in [DEVNET.md](https://github.com/karlfloersch/optimism/blob/9f679db23ac12be10049766843495a03eb2993c2/op-private-interop/docs/DEVNET.md). Installing the custom native ETH bridge implementation requires explicit send/relay permissions.

Validation on this unchanged revision:

- Fourteen targeted Go test packages pass, covering private interop, batcher, claim-follow, chain container, driver, engine, sequencing, source client, smoke and devstack.
- Ten focused Rust projection/genesis tests and 78 targeted Solidity tests pass (Foundry lite profile). Main-workspace and SP1-guest Rust formatting pass.
- Full Go lint finds two existing issues: unchecked `big.Int.Uint64` in the position resolver and import ordering in the private interop preset. The fixes prepared locally are intentionally excluded to preserve this revision.
- Current upstream `develop` has three merge conflicts with this branch, in devstack configuration/signer setup. No upstream reconciliation is included.
- Full protocol/security review, full devnet acceptance and the production-cadence soak remain outstanding for this draft.

topPRs.title: feat: add private interop cleanroom implementation
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- add the private-interop private/rendering chain pair, contracts, deterministic rendering codec, builder, and claim-follow path
- integrate the pair with op-deployer, op-batcher, op-supernode, op-interop-filter, devstack, and op-up
- add private-pair-aware interop smoke coverage and a design document
- harden the implementation after adversarial review: structurally close deposits, bind rendering inputs and emitters, cap amplification, remove the separate operator key/premine, disable the stock ETH path, and make rendering execution fully zero-fee

## `op-up --private-interop` topology

```text
                         L1 EL + beacon node
                          ^              |
                          | batches      | derives
         +----------------+---+      +---v-----------------+
         |                    |      |                     |
   normal A batcher    private-interop batcher       shared supernode
         ^                    ^                      public view: {A, B-render}
         |                    |                         |          |
 A sequencer op-node   B private op-node               |          |
         |                    |                         |          |
 A sequencer op-reth   B private op-reth         A verifier   B rendering
   public chain 901    private chain 902           op-reth       op-reth
                              ^                                     |
                              +------ `/902/claimed` ----------------+
```

- Chain A is an ordinary public OP chain with a stock batcher and proposer.
- Chain B has two different histories sharing chain ID 902: the sequenced, user-facing custom-gas-token private chain and a public, derived-only rendering with no sequencer or mempool.
- The private-interop batcher reads private B blocks, converts exported logs into claim/replay transactions, checks the rendering parent, and posts an ordinary channel to L1.
- The shared supernode derives and judges `{A, B-render}` using the stock message database and cross-safety logic. It has no private-chain access and does not know that B is a rendering.
- The only private-interop addition in the supernode is the `/902/claimed` follow endpoint. It reconstructs the committed private-B safe block reference from public rendering claims for the private op-node; it does not alter judging.
- Private B and rendering B are never P2P-peered: they deliberately have the same chain ID but different genesis hashes and block contents.
- `--smoke` runs `interopsmoke` in the same process so private receipt positions can be resolved to their canonical public rendering positions.

## Verification

- `go test ./op-batcher/batcher ./op-chain-ops/interopsmoke/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/state ./op-interop-filter/filter ./op-private-interop/... ./op-supernode/supernode/chain_container -count=1`
- focused op-deployer private-interop genesis/rollup integration tests
- 49/49 private-interop Solidity tests
- 24/24 L2-to-L2 messenger Solidity tests
- 15/15 L2 genesis Solidity tests
- `op-up --private-interop --smoke`: chain identity, native transfers, valid messages in both directions, rendered private-chain message resolution, and invalid-message reorg all pass

## Notes

This is intentionally a draft for design and security review. The stock Superchain ETH bridge smoke case is skipped on the custom-gas-token private half; that path is closed by design and `NativeMintBridge` is the sanctioned liquidity path.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: Improve OPCMv2 migration flow and harden validator checks
topPRs.author: 0xiamflux
topPRs.body:
## Context

`OPCM.migrate()` is an irreversible operation that moves independent chains onto a shared ETHLockbox, DisputeGameFactory and AnchorStateRegistry, sweeps every chain's ETH into the shared lockbox, and invalidates all outstanding withdrawal proofs. `OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator` is meant to prove afterwards that this landed correctly.

**Three main gaps**

`migrate()` could run twice. A second call drains the first shared lockbox into a new one and clears every game implementation from the shared factory, breaking every chain in the set. 

It accepted chains from any release. A chain one release behind came out with its portal, `SystemConfig` and dispute contracts upgraded, while its bridges and messengers stayed the same. `upgrade()` refuses that while `migrate()` performed it silently.

The validator's per-chain clearing checks were behind a condition that cannot hold after a successful migration, so they never ran.

## Changes

**Migrator**

- Reject chains that already have `Features.INTEROP` enabled. `migrate()` is the only thing in that sets that flag on L1, so it means
  migration already ran.
- Require every chain to be on this OPCM's release. `isPermittedMigrateSequence` accepts the same OPCM, or a replacement OPCM for the
  same release. It refuses next-major, because that would allow upgrades through the migrate function.
- Enforce the `SuperchainConfig` version floor that `_apply` already enforced.
- Grant proxy-deployment permission by name for the replacing the blanket ALL grant.

**Validator**

- Run the legacy-clearing checks unconditionally, taking each chain's pre-migration factory as input.
- Assert migration by checking anchor root, respected game type, init bonds, expected shared addresses, portal and retired-lockbox balances, and stale pauses on retired identifiers.

**Shared**

- One canonical list of the game types migration clears, in `GameTypes`.
- One encoder for `SystemConfig.initialize`, in `OPContractsManagerUtilsCaller`.
- Both sequence predicates moved into OPContractsManagerUtils. Keeping them inline pushed OPCMv2 past EIP-170.

**Test Plan**

- Every new guard proved by negative control.
- The re-entry guard was proved against real corruption first. Before the fix, a second migration one second later succeeded, wiped the shared factory's `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` implementation, and drained the shared lockbox to zero.
- size-check passes. OPCMv2 runtime is 24,553 with 23 bytes of margin.
- lint, snapshots, unused-imports and test-validation clean.

Closes #22771
